findings.title: `cagg_freshness_for_session` does not normalize `-infinity` and will crash on a never-run policy
findings.description: The new probe selects `stats.last_successful_finish` verbatim. The project's own sibling query (`_JOB_SQL` in `src/manta_trading/market/maintenance/cagg_freshness.py:68-84`) wraps the column in `nullif(s.last_successful_finish, '-infinity'::timestamptz)` specifically because "psycopg cannot load that into a datetime — it raises DataError mid-fetch", a hazard documented at length there and pinned by `test/integration/test_policy_advances_head.py:85-98`. A refresh policy that has been created but never completed a run reports `-infinity`; this query will raise `psycopg.DataError` inside `run_verify`, which only catches `RepairScanTimeout` at `scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py`'s `main` — so the operator gets a raw traceback instead of the intended `[WAIT]`/refusal path. Copy the `nullif` normalization (or reuse the existing catalog-read helper) so the probe degrades to `last_refresh=None` (conservatively stale) instead of crashing.

findings.title: The sudoers file does not cover the repair invocations the cutover script issues
findings.description: `manta-ops` claims to name "Exactly the commands those scripts issue, nothing wider", but `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:_repair` runs `sudo /opt/manta-trading/.venv/bin/python scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py <mode>` (via `cutover_common.run(..., sudo=True)`), which matches no `Cmnd_Alias` (`MT_RUN` is only `/usr/local/bin/mt-run *`). Run as `manta` with this sudoers file, the cutover dies at the first `--check` with a password prompt / `sudo: command not allowed`. Either add a `MT_REPAIR` alias for the production-interpreter repair invocation or change `_repair` to go through `mt-run` (e.g. `sudo mt-run data …` / a wrapper verb), and reconcile the header comment. Related, unverified: plain `journalctl -u mt-*` (no sudo) also needs journal-group membership for the `manta` account; I could not verify that from the repo.

findings.title: Per-chunk `fetch_session_bounds` adds a DB round trip to every minute chunk
findings.description: `_do_minute_symbol` now issues `fetch_session_bounds` once per chunk — including on the backfill phase, which walks ~69 chunks per symbol over ~13k symbols, and even for outcomes that carry no bars (where `judge_chunk_by_sessions` returns immediately). The query is small and indexed, so this is unlikely to be the pass's bottleneck next to provider calls, but hoisting the fetch to only the `SUCCESS`/`PARTIAL`-with-bars branch (or memoizing per `(symbol, chunk_start…chunk_end)` coalescence) would keep the hot loop unchanged where the new logic does not apply.

findings.title: `MT_INSTALL`'s `--ref *` wildcard over a user-writable script is effectively unrestricted root
findings.description: The sudoers wildcard permits any arguments after `--ref`, and the named script lives in the operator's own checkout (`/home/manta/source/repos/manta/trading-data/...`), so the operator account can already edit what runs as root — the rule grants root to a user who controls the payload. This is presumably a deliberate trust boundary (single-operator host), but the header's "exactly the commands those scripts issue" framing overstates the containment; worth a comment acknowledging it, or pinning the installer's checksum/ref.

findings.title: Session-predicate judgement (`judge_chunk_by_sessions`) is correct and well tested
findings.description: `bar_timestamp` mirrors `_bar_to_row`'s parsing (epoch wins, ISO fallback, UTC), `sessions_without_bars` uses `bisect_right(stamps, open)` + `<= close`, which is exactly the `(open, close]` predicate the repair's truncated-day index applies, and the pass-through cases (no bars, non-SUCCESS/PARTIAL, no judgeable session) preserve the classifier's verdict. The new unit tests cover the 2026-09-10 spillover case, the open-bar boundary, the weekend-tail promotion, and the wiring through `_do_minute_symbol`/`_run_minute_phase`/`run_minute_cycle`.

findings.title: Timer drift to 04:05 UTC is consistent across every holder
findings.description: `MINUTE_PASS_FIRING_TIMES_UTC` (04:05, 13:05), `deploy/systemd/mt-minute-pass.timer` (04:05/13:05), `test/unit/test_constants.py`, `test/unit/deploy/test_units.py`'s drift guard, and the health-check boundary tests (07:04/07:05) all agree; the Kalshi timer's collision comment was updated to match.

findings.title: Bounded firing, verify-WAIT polling, and log tee are tested with side-effect guards
findings.description: The autouse `_no_side_effects` fixture blocks real subprocesses and sleeps, and the new tests pin: stop-once-trailing-line-appears, no-stop-when-unit-ends-first, log tee content, WAIT re-polling (bounded at `VERIFY_WAIT_POLLS + 1` calls), and a WAIT verdict never counting as acceptance (exit 1). The `stale`/fresh/None semantics of `CaggFreshness` and the probe's SQL shape are pinned in `test_repair_921.py`.
